O*NET 29-1141.00 defines registered nurses as an occupation that assesses patient needs, develops and implements nursing care plans, maintains medical records and provides nursing care, requiring licensure or registration.

Core tasks include recording vital signs, observing condition changes, administering medication under medical orders and monitoring responses, coordinating nursing teams, educating patients and handing over.

values: Materials and scenario | A1–A5 are entirely fictional, de-identified paper cases, not diagnosis, treatment or medication instructions

Complete an N1 handover in 30 minutes: 5 minutes reading records, 20 minutes checking conflicts and risks, and 5 minutes writing the escalation; do not use it to administer medication or manage actual patients.

A1 | The handover form gives patient code N1; the bedside wristband says N2. There are no actual names, identity card numbers or medical record numbers. Identity is unconfirmed; pause affected patient-specific actions.
A2 | The paper order list contains versions V1 and V2; V2 issuance status has not been checked. Do not compare medication doses or select a version to execute.

A3 | The handover record gives a temperature of 37.0°C at 09:00, and 38.2°C at 10:00. These are fictional observations only. Record times and sources and report changes to authorized clinical personnel; do not independently diagnose the cause.
A4 | One version of the allergy field says “to be checked”; another is blank. Blank does not mean “no allergies”; first check original records and the patient's own report.

A5 | The paper handover requires four unresolved items concerning identity, orders, observations and allergies, with responsible personnel. Only after the recipient confirms may next steps be decided under actual institutional procedures.
Task and deliverables
List the N1/N2 identity conflict, unchecked V1/V2 order versions, the 1.2°C paper difference from 37.0 to 38.2, and the allergy field conflict.

Submit a one-page abnormality handover form, recording original times, risks, scope of paused actions, escalation recipients and items awaiting confirmation for each item; do not write diagnoses, doses or treatment.
Reference answer (complete independently before reading)
The N1 and N2 identity labels conflict; initially keep identity unconfirmed, stop affected patient-specific actions and check authoritative identity sources.
V2 issuance status has not been checked; a newer version cannot be presumed valid, and a blank allergy field cannot mean no allergies.
38.2 minus 37.0 gives a 1.2°C change on paper; do not diagnose or intervene based on the difference. Preserve original records and refer to authorized personnel for assessment.
Boundaries and review

N1/N2, temperatures and order versions are entirely fictional. Actual patient identification, medication and treatment require licensed nursing personnel acting under institutional procedures and valid orders; this exercise confers no qualification to practice.

description.text: What registered nurses do, how to check Chinese practice registration and US wage and employment data, with a fictional nursing handover exercise, patient safety and AI boundaries.

subject.name: Registered Nurses
subject.summary: Assess patients' conditions, develop or implement nursing care plans, provide authorized nursing care, medication administration and treatment, document changes in condition, and hand over to the healthcare team. Practice registration, patient identification checks, medical orders, infection protection and escalation of abnormalities are key boundaries; countries' education and licensing systems must not be treated as mutually recognized.
